03What We Do

Six areas of care.

Safe Care

Supervised, family-style residential care for children who currently have no safe alternative, with consistent house staff rather than rotating shifts.

Education

School enrolment, fees, uniforms and supplies are arranged and tracked for each child, with tutoring support for those behind grade level.

Health & Wellbeing

Routine medical checkups, nutrition, and referral to specialist care when a child arrives with an unmet health need.

Family Support

Where a child has traceable family, we work with them directly — assessing the home situation and providing support aimed at safe reunification.

Family Reintegration

A structured, monitored process for returning a child to family or kinship care when it is assessed as safe, with follow-up after placement.

Life Skills

Practical and vocational preparation for older children moving toward independence, including budgeting, work-readiness and mentorship.

04How We Support Children

Every child's case is handled individually.

01

Referral

A child is referred by a guardian, local authority, or community contact.

02

Assessment

Our team assesses the child's situation, safety, and family circumstances before any placement decision.

03

Safe Care

If residential care is needed, the child is placed in a supervised home with education and health support.

04

Family / Long-Term Planning

We work toward the most appropriate long-term outcome for that specific child — which may include family reunification.

05

Transition & Follow-Up

When a child leaves our care, we follow up to support a stable transition, whether to family or independence.

Residential care is not the outcome for every child we work with, and it is not intended to be permanent. Each case is reassessed on an ongoing basis, with family or kinship placement considered first where it can be done safely.

05Our Approach

Family-style care, individually planned.

We structure care around consistent relationships rather than institutional routine — the same house parents, the same home, the same daily rhythm for each child, for as long as they are in our care.

Every decision about a child's placement, education, and eventual transition is made individually, reviewed regularly, and documented.

  • Individual case planningEach child has a documented care and transition plan, reviewed on a regular basis.
  • Family-first, where safeFamily or kinship placement is prioritized over long-term residential care when it can be done safely.
  • Continuity of staffChildren are cared for by consistent house staff rather than rotating personnel.
  • AccountabilityCare decisions and finances are subject to internal review. [INSERT EXTERNAL AUDIT / OVERSIGHT DETAILS IF AVAILABLE]

08Safeguarding

Children's safety comes first.

Safe Haven Children's Home is committed to protecting every child in our care. This includes:

  • Physical safety and appropriate supervision at all times
  • Dignity and respectful treatment of every child
  • Privacy and confidentiality of children's personal information
  • Responsible photography — consent-based, no identifying details published without permission
  • Vetted staff and volunteers, with clear conduct standards
  • A clear process for reporting safeguarding concerns

POLICYChild Safeguarding

Child Safeguarding

Every child in our care has the right to safety, dignity, privacy and protection from abuse, exploitation and neglect.

Policy owner: [INSERT VERIFIED SAFEGUARDING LEAD] · Last reviewed: [INSERT REVIEW DATE]

01

Our safeguarding commitment

Safe Haven Children's Home is committed to protecting the children in our care from all forms of harm. Safeguarding is the responsibility of every member of staff, every volunteer, and every visitor to our premises — not a single department or individual.

This page describes our current safeguarding practice. Where a formal written policy, external accreditation, or third-party audit exists, it is referenced below. Where it does not yet exist, this is marked clearly rather than implied.

[INSERT VERIFIED POLICY — link to or summary of the organization's full written Child Safeguarding Policy document, if one exists]

02

Keeping children safe

Day-to-day care is structured around consistent supervision, predictable routines, and known, vetted adults. Specific measures include:

  • Consistent house staff rather than rotating or unknown personnel
  • Restricted, logged access to residential areas for anyone outside core staff
  • A named adult each child can go to with a concern
  • Regular health and welfare checks for every child in care

[INSERT VERIFIED POLICY — supervision ratios, on-site security measures, and emergency procedures specific to the facility]

03

Staff and volunteer standards

All staff and volunteers are expected to model respectful, appropriate conduct at all times, including:

  • No adult is ever alone with a single child in a closed or private space
  • No physical punishment or degrading treatment, under any circumstance
  • No private communication, gift-giving, or social media contact with a child outside official channels
  • Any physical contact is limited to what is necessary for care, and appropriate to the child's age

Breaches of these standards are treated as safeguarding incidents and are subject to [INSERT VERIFIED POLICY — disciplinary and reporting procedure].

04

Recruitment and screening

All staff and long-term volunteers who will have contact with children go through a screening process before starting work, and are expected to complete safeguarding orientation before unsupervised contact with children.

[INSERT VERIFIED POLICY — background check provider, police clearance requirements, reference checks, and training/orientation program specifics]

05

Photography and media

We limit and control how children are photographed, filmed, or named in any public material, including our website, social media, and materials shared with donors or partners.

  • No child's full name is published alongside their photograph
  • Photography of children requires documented consent from a parent, guardian, or authorized official
  • Images that could reveal a child's location, school, or identifying routine are avoided
  • Children may decline to be photographed at any time
On this website specifically: we do not publish children's names, personal histories, or identifying details anywhere on this site. Public-facing photography on this site is limited to staff, facilities, and general environments — not close, identifiable images of individual children.
06

Privacy and confidentiality

Information about a child's background, family circumstances, health, or legal status is treated as confidential. It is shared only with staff, officials, or professionals who need it to provide care or make decisions in the child's interest.

[INSERT VERIFIED POLICY — data protection practices, record-keeping and retention, and who has access to case files]

07

Visitors and volunteers

Anyone visiting Safe Haven — including donors, partner organizations, and short-term volunteers — is expected to follow our visitor protocol:

  • Sign in and out, and remain with an assigned staff member at all times
  • No unsupervised contact with children
  • No photography without prior authorization

[INSERT VERIFIED POLICY — formal visitor policy document or volunteer agreement, if one exists]

[Photo placeholder — staff or facility image, not children]
08

Reporting a concern

Anyone — staff, a child, a family member, a volunteer, or a member of the public — can and should report a safeguarding concern. You do not need to be certain a child is being harmed to raise a concern; a suspicion is enough.

Report a Safeguarding Concern

Concerns are handled by our safeguarding lead and treated confidentially. If a child is in immediate danger, contact local emergency services first.
